questions.question:
Give an example of a metal which

(i) is a liquid at room temperature.

(ii) can be easily cut with a knife.

(iii) is the best conductor of heat.

(iv) is a poor conductor of heat.
answer_steps: (i) Mercury (ii) Sodium (or potassium)
(iii) Silver (iv) Lead (or mercury)

questions.question: Explain the meanings of malleable and ductile.
answer_steps: Malleable: can be beaten into thin sheets (like aluminium foil).
Ductile: can be drawn into thin wires (like copper wire).

questions.question: Why is sodium kept immersed in kerosene oil?
answer_steps: Sodium reacts so vigorously with oxygen and moisture in air that it catches fire.
Kerosene does not react with sodium and keeps air and water away from it.

questions.question:
Write equations for the reactions of

(i) iron with steam

(ii) calcium and potassium with water
answer_steps: (i) $\mathrm{3Fe(s) + 4H_{2}O(g) \rightarrow Fe_{3}O_{4}(s) + 4H_{2}(g)}$
(ii) $\mathrm{Ca(s) + 2H_{2}O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_{2}(aq) + H_{2}(g)}$
$\mathrm{2K(s) + 2H_{2}O(l) \rightarrow 2KOH(aq) + H_{2}(g)}$

questions.question:
Samples of four metals A, B, C and D were added one by one to the following solutions.

Metal A: no reaction with iron(II) sulphate; displacement with copper(II) sulphate.

Metal B: displacement with iron(II) sulphate; no reaction with zinc sulphate.

Metal C: no reaction with iron(II) sulphate, copper(II) sulphate or zinc sulphate; displacement with silver nitrate.

Metal D: no reaction with any of the four solutions.

(i) Which is the most reactive metal?

(ii) What would you observe if B is added to a solution of copper(II) sulphate?

(iii) Arrange the metals A, B, C and D in the order of decreasing reactivity.
answer_steps: (i) B: it displaces iron, so it is the most reactive of the four.
(ii) B displaces copper: the blue colour fades and a reddish-brown layer of copper forms.
(iii) B > A > C > D

questions.question: Which gas is produced when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to a reactive metal? Write the chemical reaction when iron reacts with dilute H₂SO₄.
answer_steps: Hydrogen gas.
$\mathrm{Fe(s) + H_{2}SO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow FeSO_{4}(aq) + H_{2}(g)}$

questions.question: What would you observe when zinc is added to a solution of iron(II) sulphate? Write the chemical reaction that takes place.
answer_steps: Zinc is more reactive than iron, so the pale green colour fades and iron is deposited.
$\mathrm{Zn(s) + FeSO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_{4}(aq) + Fe(s)}$

questions.question:
(i) Write the electron-dot structures for sodium, oxygen and magnesium.

(ii) Show the formation of Na₂O and MgO by the transfer of electrons.

(iii) What are the ions present in these compounds?
answer_steps: (i) Sodium (2, 8, 1) has one dot around its symbol; oxygen (2, 6) has six dots; magnesium (2, 8, 2) has two dots.

(ii) Each of two sodium atoms gives one electron to oxygen: $\mathrm{Na \rightarrow Na^{+} + e^{-}}$ (twice) and $\mathrm{O + 2e^{-} \rightarrow O^{2-}}$, giving Na₂O. Magnesium gives two electrons to oxygen: $\mathrm{Mg \rightarrow Mg^{2+} + 2e^{-}}$ and $\mathrm{O + 2e^{-} \rightarrow O^{2-}}$, giving MgO.
(iii) Na₂O: Na⁺ and O²⁻ ions. MgO: Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ ions.

questions.question: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?
answer_steps: The ions are held together by strong forces of electrostatic attraction.
A lot of energy is needed to overcome these forces, so the melting points are high.

questions.question:
Define the following terms.

(i) Mineral

(ii) Ore

(iii) Gangue
answer_steps: (i) Mineral: an element or compound that occurs naturally in the earth's crust.
(ii) Ore: a mineral from which a metal can be extracted profitably.
(iii) Gangue: the earth, sand and other impurities present in the ore.

questions.question: Which two metals are found in nature in the free state?
questions.explanation: Metals at the bottom of the reactivity series are so unreactive that they occur free.
option_feedback: They are too reactive to occur free.
They are found as oxides, sulphides or carbonates.
They are reactive and found in compounds.
Correct!

questions.question: What chemical process is used for obtaining a metal from its oxide?
questions.explanation: Removing oxygen from the oxide is reduction, for example $\mathrm{ZnO(s) + C(s) \rightarrow Zn(s) + CO(g)}$
option_feedback: Calcination makes the oxide from a carbonate.
That is an acid-base reaction.
Correct!
Removing oxygen is reduction.

questions.question: Metallic oxides of zinc, magnesium and copper were heated with the following metals: zinc, magnesium and copper. In which cases will you find displacement reactions taking place?
answer_steps: A metal displaces another only if it is more reactive: Mg > Zn > Cu.
Zinc with copper oxide: $\mathrm{Zn + CuO \rightarrow ZnO + Cu}$
Magnesium with zinc oxide and with copper oxide: $\mathrm{Mg + ZnO \rightarrow MgO + Zn}$; $\mathrm{Mg + CuO \rightarrow MgO + Cu}$

questions.question: Which metals do not corrode easily?
questions.explanation: Gold and platinum are very unreactive, so moisture and air do not attack them.
option_feedback: They react at once with air.
Copper turns green and lead tarnishes.
Correct!
Iron rusts; zinc slowly corrodes.

questions.question: What are alloys?
answer_steps: An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or of a metal and a non-metal.
Examples: brass (copper and zinc), stainless steel (iron, nickel and chromium).

questions.question: Which of the following pairs will give displacement reactions?
questions.explanation: Only copper is more reactive than the metal in the salt (silver).
option_feedback: Copper is less reactive than sodium.
Aluminium is less reactive than magnesium.
Silver is less reactive than iron.
Correct!

questions.question: Which of the following methods is suitable for preventing an iron frying pan from rusting?
questions.explanation: Each of them keeps air and moisture away from the iron.
option_feedback: It works, but so do the others.
It works, but so do the others.
It works, but so do the others.
Correct!

questions.question: An element reacts with oxygen to give a compound with a high melting point. This compound is also soluble in water. The element is likely to be
questions.explanation: Calcium oxide is an ionic compound with a high melting point, and it dissolves in water.
option_feedback: Correct!
Carbon forms gaseous oxides.
Silicon dioxide does not dissolve in water.
Iron oxide does not dissolve in water.

questions.question: Food cans are coated with tin and not with zinc because
options: zinc has a higher melting point than tin.
zinc is more reactive than tin.
zinc is less reactive than tin.
questions.explanation: Zinc could react with acids in the food; tin is less reactive.
option_feedback: The reason is reactivity, not cost.
Melting point is not the reason.
Correct!
Zinc is more reactive than tin.

questions.question:
You are given a hammer, a battery, a bulb, wires and a switch.

(a) How could you use them to distinguish between samples of metals and non-metals?

(b) Assess the usefulness of these tests in distinguishing between metals and non-metals.
answer_steps: (a) Hammer each sample: metals flatten into sheets (malleable); non-metals break into pieces.
Connect each sample in a circuit with the battery, bulb and switch: metals make the bulb glow; non-metals do not.
(b) These tests are useful, but there are exceptions: graphite (a non-metal) conducts electricity, and mercury is a liquid metal that cannot be hammered.

questions.question: What are amphoteric oxides? Give two examples of amphoteric oxides.
answer_steps: Metal oxides that react with both acids and bases to give salt and water are amphoteric oxides.
Examples: aluminium oxide and zinc oxide.

questions.question: Name two metals which will displace hydrogen from dilute acids, and two metals which will not.
answer_steps: Displace hydrogen: zinc and magnesium (metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series).
Do not: copper and silver (below hydrogen).

questions.question: In the electrolytic refining of a metal M, what would you take as the anode, the cathode and the electrolyte?
answer_steps: Anode: a thick block of impure metal M.
Cathode: a thin strip of pure metal M.
Electrolyte: a solution of a soluble salt of M.

questions.question:
Pratyush took sulphur powder on a spatula and heated it. He collected the gas evolved by inverting a test tube over it.

(a) What will be the action of the gas on (i) dry litmus paper? (ii) moist litmus paper?

(b) Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction taking place.
answer_steps: (a) (i) No change on dry litmus paper.
(ii) Moist blue litmus turns red: sulphur dioxide dissolves to form an acid, $\mathrm{SO_{2}(g) + H_{2}O(l) \rightarrow H_{2}SO_{3}(aq)}$
(b) $\mathrm{S(s) + O_{2}(g) \rightarrow SO_{2}(g)}$

questions.question: State two ways to prevent the rusting of iron.
answer_steps: Painting, oiling or greasing the iron.
Galvanising (coating with zinc), or making alloys such as stainless steel.

questions.question: What type of oxides are formed when non-metals combine with oxygen?
answer_steps: Acidic oxides, such as sulphur dioxide and carbon dioxide.
Some are neutral, such as carbon monoxide and water.

questions.question:
Give reasons

(a) Platinum, gold and silver are used to make jewellery.

(b) Sodium, potassium and lithium are stored under oil.

(c) Aluminium is a highly reactive metal, yet it is used to make utensils for cooking.

(d) Carbonate and sulphide ores are usually converted into oxides during the process of extraction.
answer_steps: (a) They are lustrous, malleable and ductile, and so unreactive that they do not corrode.
(b) They react vigorously with air and water and may catch fire; oil keeps air and water away.
(c) Aluminium is protected by a thin layer of aluminium oxide that stops further reaction; it is also light and a good conductor of heat.
(d) It is easier to obtain a metal from its oxide by reduction than from its carbonate or sulphide.
For example: $\mathrm{2ZnS(s) + 3O_{2}(g) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2ZnO(s) + 2SO_{2}(g)}$, then $\mathrm{ZnO(s) + C(s) \rightarrow Zn(s) + CO(g)}$

questions.question: You must have seen tarnished copper vessels being cleaned with lemon or tamarind juice. Explain why these sour substances are effective in cleaning the vessels.
answer_steps: Tarnished copper has a coating of basic copper carbonate (and copper oxide), which is basic.
Lemon and tamarind contain acids that react with and dissolve this coating, so the vessel shines again.

questions.question: Differentiate between metal and non-metal on the basis of their chemical properties.
answer_steps: Metals form basic (or amphoteric) oxides; non-metals form acidic or neutral oxides.
Metals above hydrogen displace hydrogen from dilute acids; non-metals do not.
Metals lose electrons to form positive ions; non-metals gain electrons to form negative ions.

questions.question: A man went door to door posing as a goldsmith. He promised to bring back the glitter of old and dull gold ornaments. An unsuspecting lady gave a set of gold bangles to him which he dipped in a particular solution. The bangles sparkled like new but their weight was reduced drastically. The lady was upset but after a futile argument the man beat a hasty retreat. Can you play the detective to find out the nature of the solution he had used?
answer_steps: He used aqua regia: a freshly prepared mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and concentrated nitric acid in the ratio 3 : 1.
Aqua regia dissolves gold, so the outer layer dissolved away, the bangles shone, and their weight decreased.

questions.question: Give reasons why copper is used to make hot water tanks and not steel (an alloy of iron).
answer_steps: Copper does not react with cold water, hot water or steam, so it does not corrode.
Iron in steel reacts with steam and rusts; copper is also a better conductor of heat.

questions.question:
Four statements about the reactions of oxides with dilute hydrochloric acid and aqueous sodium hydroxide are listed.

I. Aluminium oxide reacts with both dilute hydrochloric acid and aqueous sodium hydroxide.

II. Calcium oxide reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid and aqueous sodium hydroxide.

III. Zinc oxide reacts with both dilute hydrochloric acid and aqueous sodium hydroxide.

IV. Sulphur dioxide does not react with either dilute hydrochloric acid or aqueous sodium hydroxide.

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide and zinc oxide are amphoteric. Calcium oxide is basic (it does not react with NaOH) and sulphur dioxide is acidic (it reacts with NaOH).
option_feedback: Calcium oxide is basic; it does not react with NaOH.
Correct!
Calcium oxide does not react with NaOH, and SO₂ does react with NaOH.
Sulphur dioxide, an acidic oxide, reacts with NaOH.

questions.question: An iron nail is added to each of two test tubes P and Q containing aqueous copper(II) sulphate and aqueous silver nitrate respectively. Which of the following observations is correct?
options: In test tube P the iron nail gets a blue coating and in test tube Q there is no reaction.
The iron nail gets a brown coating in test tube P and a silver coating in test tube Q.
There is no reaction in either test tube P or Q.
There is no reaction in test tube P but a silver coating forms on the iron nail in test tube Q.
questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than both copper and silver, so it displaces copper (brown) in P and silver in Q.
option_feedback: Copper is brown, not blue, and iron also displaces silver.
Correct!
Iron is more reactive than copper and silver.
Iron also displaces copper.

questions.question:
A teacher clamped an aluminium wire on a stand and fixed a pin to the free end using wax. He heated the wire from the clamped end, and the pin fell off.

A. If the teacher replaces the aluminium wire by a silver wire, will the students' observation change? Justify your answer.

B. Will the aluminium wire melt? Give reason for your answer.
answer_steps: A. The pin will still drop, but sooner, because silver is a better conductor of heat than aluminium.
B. No: metals have high melting points, and the burner does not reach the melting point of aluminium.

questions.question:
An element 'X' is stored in kerosene, and cannot be extracted from its ore using a reducing agent. 'X' forms an ionic compound on reaction with chlorine.

(i) Can we store 'X' in water? Give reason to support your answer.

(ii) Identify element 'X'. Name the process used and write the equations for the extraction of 'X' from its ore.
answer_steps: (i) No: X is highly reactive and reacts violently with water; it would catch fire.
(ii) X is sodium (potassium is also correct). It is extracted by electrolytic reduction of molten sodium chloride.
Cathode: $\mathrm{Na^{+} + e^{-} \rightarrow Na}$; anode: $\mathrm{2Cl^{-} \rightarrow Cl_{2} + 2e^{-}}$

questions.question:
The domes of many buildings in Europe are made of copper. These domes now appear greenish in colour.

(i) Why do the domes appear greenish though copper is orange-red in colour?

(ii) In your opinion, should the copper domes be replaced by iron domes to overcome the problem of change of colour?

(iii) Domes used to be made from thin sheets of metal. Why did the ancient architects use copper to make domes?
answer_steps: (i) Copper corrodes slowly in moist air to form basic copper carbonate, which is green.
(ii) No: iron would rust, and the flaky rust would expose more iron, weakening the dome. The green layer on copper protects it from further corrosion.
(iii) Copper is highly malleable, so thin sheets can be shaped into a dome.

questions.question:
Oxygen can combine with both metals and non-metals. It combines with calcium to form CaO and with carbon to form CO₂.

(a) What type of bond is formed between carbon and oxygen?

(b) Identify the type of bond formed between calcium and oxygen.

(c) Which of the above compounds will be a good conductor of electricity in molten state and why?

(d) Comment on the physical state (solid, liquid or gas) of CaO and CO₂.

(e) What is the valency of carbon in CO₂?
answer_steps: (a) Covalent bond (sharing of electrons).
(b) Ionic bond (transfer of electrons from calcium to oxygen).
(c) CaO: in the molten state its ions are free to move.
(d) CaO is a solid (strong ionic forces); CO₂ is a gas (weak forces between molecules).

questions.question:
Metal X is found in nature as its sulphide ore XS. This metal is used in the galvanisation of iron articles.

(a) Identify the metal X.

(b) Explain, with chemical equations, how this sulphide ore XS is converted into the metal X.
answer_steps: (a) X is zinc (ore: zinc blende, ZnS).
(b) Roasting in excess air: $\mathrm{2ZnS(s) + 3O_{2}(g) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2ZnO(s) + 2SO_{2}(g)}$
Reduction with carbon: $\mathrm{ZnO(s) + C(s) \rightarrow Zn(s) + CO(g)}$

questions.question: ____ is the chemical formula of cinnabar.
questions.explanation: Cinnabar, the ore of mercury, is mercury sulphide; ZnS is zinc blende and Cu₂S is copper glance.
option_feedback: Correct!
That is zinc blende.
That is copper glance.

questions.question: State whether the following statement is true or false: Solder is an alloy of lead and tin.
questions.explanation: True: solder is an alloy of lead and tin with a low melting point, used for welding electrical wires.
option_feedback: Correct! True: solder is an alloy of lead and tin with a low melting point, used for welding electrical wires.
Not quite. True: solder is an alloy of lead and tin with a low melting point, used for welding electrical wires.

questions.question:
The electronic configurations of two elements X and Y are: X = 2, 8, 1 and Y = 2, 8, 7.

(a) Identify the metal and write its name.

(b) Identify the non-metal and write its name.

(c) Which ionic compound is formed by X and Y?
answer_steps: (a) X is the metal: sodium (it loses one electron).
(b) Y is the non-metal: chlorine (it gains one electron).
(c) Sodium chloride, NaCl: $\mathrm{2Na + Cl_{2} \rightarrow 2NaCl}$

questions.question:
In an experiment, iron nails are kept in three test tubes: A with tap water (air and water), B with boiled distilled water covered by oil (no air), and C with anhydrous calcium chloride (dry air).

(a) In which test tube will the colour of the iron nail change?

(b) Name the chemical reaction associated with it.

(c) Write the essential conditions required for this reaction.
answer_steps: (a) Test tube A.
(b) Rusting of iron (corrosion).
(c) Both air (oxygen) and water (moisture) must be present.

questions.question:
Give an example of a metal which

(a) melts if you keep it on your palm.

(b) can be easily cut with a knife.

(c) is found in nature in the free state.
answer_steps: (a) Gallium (or caesium).
(b) Sodium (or potassium).
(c) Gold (or platinum).

questions.question: Which non-metal is lustrous?
questions.explanation: Iodine has a shiny lustre although it is a non-metal.
option_feedback: Sulphur is dull yellow.
Phosphorus is not lustrous.
Coal is dull.
Correct!

questions.question: Which form of carbon is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Graphite conducts electricity; diamond does not.
option_feedback: Coal is a poor conductor.
Charcoal powder is a poor conductor.
Correct!
Diamond does not conduct electricity.

questions.question: Which metal reacts with cold water so vigorously that the hydrogen catches fire?
questions.explanation: Potassium (like sodium) reacts violently with cold water.
option_feedback: Copper does not react with water.
Correct!
Magnesium reacts only with hot water.
Iron reacts only with steam.

questions.question: Calcium floats when it reacts with water because:
options: bubbles of hydrogen stick to its surface
questions.explanation: The hydrogen bubbles make it float.
option_feedback: Correct!
Calcium is denser than water.
It does not melt in water.
The bubbles, not an oxide layer, make it float.

questions.question: The process of heating a carbonate ore in limited air is called:
questions.explanation: Calcination is used for carbonate ores; roasting for sulphide ores.
option_feedback: Roasting uses excess air, for sulphide ores.
Smelting is reduction at high temperature.
Refining purifies the metal.
Correct!

questions.question: In the thermite reaction, the reducing agent is:
questions.explanation: Aluminium removes oxygen from iron oxide: $\mathrm{Fe_{2}O_{3}(s) + 2Al(s) \rightarrow 2Fe(l) + Al_{2}O_{3}(s)}$
option_feedback: There is no carbon in the thermite reaction.
There is no hydrogen in the thermite reaction.
Correct!
Iron oxide is reduced; it is the oxidising agent.

questions.question: Highly reactive metals such as sodium are extracted by:
questions.explanation: Carbon cannot reduce them, so electrolysis is used.
option_feedback: Roasting only converts sulphides to oxides.
Correct!
Carbon cannot reduce such reactive metals.
That works only for metals like mercury.

questions.question: 22 carat gold contains:
options: 22 parts gold and 2 parts silver or copper
questions.explanation: Pure gold is 24 carat; 22 carat gold is alloyed with 2 parts silver or copper to make it harder.
option_feedback: Correct!
The total is 24 parts.
Pure gold is 24 carat.
It is the other way round.

questions.question: Which property is shown by ionic compounds?
questions.explanation: Strong forces between ions give them high melting points.
option_feedback: Ions cannot move in the solid.
They dissolve in water, not kerosene.
Their boiling points are high.
Correct!

questions.question: Galvanisation is coating iron with:
questions.explanation: Galvanised iron has a coating of zinc.
option_feedback: Tin plating is used for food cans.
That is chrome plating.
Copper is not used for galvanising.
Correct!

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Sodium is stored under kerosene.

**Reason (R):** Sodium reacts vigorously with oxygen and water.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Kerosene keeps air and water away from the reactive metal: R explains A.
option_feedback: Correct! A is true: kerosene keeps air and water away from sodium. R is true: its high reactivity is exactly why it is kept under kerosene.
R does explain A: its high reactivity is exactly why it is kept under kerosene.
Check the Reason again: it is true, because its high reactivity is exactly why it is kept under kerosene.
Check the Assertion again: it is true, because kerosene keeps air and water away from sodium.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Copper reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to give hydrogen.

**Reason (R):** Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: A is false: copper does not give hydrogen with dilute HCl. R is true.
option_feedback: Check the Assertion again: it is false, because copper does not give hydrogen with dilute HCl.
Check the Assertion again: it is false, because copper does not give hydrogen with dilute HCl.
Check the Assertion again: it is false, because copper does not give hydrogen with dilute HCl.
Correct! A is false: copper does not give hydrogen with dilute HCl. R is true: copper lies below hydrogen in the series.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Ionic compounds conduct electricity in the molten state.

**Reason (R):** In the molten state, the ions are free to move.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Moving ions carry the current: R explains A.
option_feedback: Correct! A is true: molten ionic compounds conduct. R is true: moving ions are exactly what carry the current.
R does explain A: moving ions are exactly what carry the current.
Check the Reason again: it is true, because moving ions are exactly what carry the current.
Check the Assertion again: it is true, because molten ionic compounds conduct.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Aluminium oxide is an amphoteric oxide.

**Reason (R):** Aluminium is a good conductor of heat.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: Both are true, but conduction of heat does not explain why the oxide reacts with both acids and bases.
option_feedback: Both are true, but R is not the reason A is true: it is true, but it does not explain the amphoteric nature of the oxide.
Correct! A is true: aluminium oxide reacts with both acids and bases. R is true: it is true, but it does not explain the amphoteric nature of the oxide.
Check the Reason again: it is true, because it is true, but it does not explain the amphoteric nature of the oxide.
Check the Assertion again: it is true, because aluminium oxide reacts with both acids and bases.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Pure gold is used for making ornaments.

**Reason (R):** Pure gold is very soft.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: A is false: pure gold is too soft, so 22 carat gold is used. R is true.
option_feedback: Check the Assertion again: it is false, because ornaments use 22 carat gold, not pure gold.
Check the Assertion again: it is false, because ornaments use 22 carat gold, not pure gold.
Check the Assertion again: it is false, because ornaments use 22 carat gold, not pure gold.
Correct! A is false: ornaments use 22 carat gold, not pure gold. R is true: pure gold is too soft to keep its shape.

questions.question: Show the formation of sodium chloride by the transfer of electrons.
answer_steps: Sodium loses one electron: $\mathrm{Na \rightarrow Na^{+} + e^{-}}$
Chlorine gains it: $\mathrm{Cl + e^{-} \rightarrow Cl^{-}}$. The oppositely charged ions attract to form Na⁺Cl⁻.

questions.question: What is the thermite reaction? Give one use.
answer_steps: The highly exothermic reduction of iron oxide by aluminium: $\mathrm{Fe_{2}O_{3}(s) + 2Al(s) \rightarrow 2Fe(l) + Al_{2}O_{3}(s)}$
The molten iron is used to join railway tracks and cracked machine parts.

questions.question: How is mercury obtained from its ore cinnabar? Write the equations.
answer_steps: Mercury is low in the reactivity series, so heating alone is enough.
Cinnabar is heated in air: $\mathrm{2HgS(s) + 3O_{2}(g) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2HgO(s) + 2SO_{2}(g)}$
On further heating, mercury oxide decomposes: $\mathrm{2HgO(s) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2Hg(l) + O_{2}(g)}$

questions.question: Arrange magnesium, potassium, copper and zinc in decreasing order of reactivity. What would you observe when zinc is added to copper sulphate solution? Write the equation.
answer_steps: K > Mg > Zn > Cu.
The blue colour of the solution fades and a reddish-brown layer of copper forms on the zinc.
$\mathrm{Zn(s) + CuSO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_{4}(aq) + Cu(s)}$

questions.question: Describe, with a labelled description, the electrolytic refining of copper. What is anode mud?
answer_steps: The anode is a thick block of impure copper; the cathode is a thin strip of pure copper.
The electrolyte is acidified copper sulphate solution.
When current flows, copper dissolves from the anode into the solution, and an equal amount of pure copper is deposited on the cathode.
Soluble impurities go into the solution.
Insoluble impurities, such as silver and gold, settle at the bottom below the anode: this is the anode mud.

questions.question: Explain, with equations, the extraction of a metal of medium reactivity such as zinc from (i) its sulphide ore (ii) its carbonate ore. Why can carbon not be used to extract sodium?
answer_steps: (i) Zinc blende is roasted: $\mathrm{2ZnS(s) + 3O_{2}(g) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2ZnO(s) + 2SO_{2}(g)}$
(ii) Calamine is calcined: $\mathrm{ZnCO_{3}(s) \xrightarrow{\Delta} ZnO(s) + CO_{2}(g)}$
The zinc oxide is reduced with carbon: $\mathrm{ZnO(s) + C(s) \rightarrow Zn(s) + CO(g)}$
The zinc can be purified by electrolytic refining.
Sodium is more reactive than carbon and has a greater affinity for oxygen, so carbon cannot reduce its compounds; electrolysis is used.

questions.question:
Neha's school is near the sea. The iron gate rusts quickly, but the steel handrail labelled 'stainless' does not. The electrician uses solder to join wires, and her grandmother's bangles are 22 carat gold.

(i) What two conditions are needed for iron to rust? (1)

(ii) Name the metals mixed with iron in stainless steel. (1)

(iii) Why is solder suitable for joining electrical wires? OR Why is 22 carat gold used for ornaments instead of 24 carat gold? (2)
answer_steps: (i) Air (oxygen) and water (moisture).
(ii) Nickel and chromium.
(iii) Solder is an alloy of lead and tin with a low melting point, so it melts easily and joins the wires. OR Pure (24 carat) gold is too soft; adding 2 parts silver or copper makes it harder.

questions.question:
Students placed small pieces of four metals P, Q, R and S in cold water. P reacted violently and caught fire. Q did not react with cold water but reacted with hot water. R reacted only with steam. S did not react even with steam.

(i) Which metal is the most reactive? (1)

(ii) Arrange the four metals in decreasing order of reactivity. (1)

(iii) If R is iron, write the equation for its reaction with steam. OR If S is copper, why is it used for hot water tanks? (2)
answer_steps: (i) P.
(ii) P > Q > R > S.
(iii) $\mathrm{3Fe(s) + 4H_{2}O(g) \rightarrow Fe_{3}O_{4}(s) + 4H_{2}(g)}$ OR Copper does not react with water or steam, so it does not corrode, and it conducts heat well.
